notes: The third-generation Echo Dot with its external plug-in power adapter. Teardowns disagree on the memory chips, so check the board before relying on the memory readings.

gaps: Memory readings conflict. iFixit (used): Micron MT29F4G08ABAFAH4-IT:F NAND and Samsung K4B2G1646F-BYMA DDR3. The 2019 blog: one Samsung package KMFN60012M-B214. The 2020 clock-version blog: the same NAND with Micron MT41K128M16JT-107 DDR3. A user-edited wiki: Samsung KMFJ20005A-B213 for both.
Model number and FCC ID are not set: no teardown names them. fccid.io's 2AOAG-3668 is listed as Moxham L.L.C. Digital Media Receiver, model 3668, not as an Echo Dot.
The Wi-Fi chip MT7658 agrees across iFixit and the 2019 blog (which writes MT7658CSN), but iFixit puts it on the bottom board and the blog on the top board; no board is claimed.
The adapter ratings come from the text of a third-party repair blog, not Amazon; the post does not say they were read off the label.
The speaker size is from NaijaTechGuide only; no source read gives output power.
The two TLV320ADC3101 ADCs named in the 2019 blog are not recorded.
No public datasheet was found for the MT8516, MT7658 or the memory chips. Mouser's IS31FL3236 datasheet link returned an access-denied page, so it is not cited.
method: iFixit 'Amazon Echo Dot 3rd Generation Teardown' (guide 138560), read through the iFixit API: step 5 chip IDs and step 8 Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip.
Brian Dorey, 'Echo Dot 3rd Gen Digging Deeper' (2019): amplifier, LED driver, LEDs and microphones.
Brian Dorey, 'Echo Dot 3rd gen smart speaker with clock teardown' (2020): memory conflict only.
NaijaTechGuide, Echo Dot (3rd Gen) specs page: speaker size and microphone count.
Tom's Tek Stop (third-party repair blog), Echo Dot 3rd generation power adapter page: model and ratings, described as the wall plug supplied with the speaker.
TechInfoDepot wiki page for the Echo Dot (user-edited) and fccid.io 2AOAG-3668: conflict notes only.
TI TAS2770 datasheet (SLASEM6E) opened and names the chip.
Not usable: Mouser's IS31FL3236 datasheet (access denied).

comps.spec: MediaTek MT8516 quad-core Cortex-A35 applications processor, up to 1.3 GHz (iFixit chip ID step)
Micron MT29F4G08ABAFAH4-IT:F 4 Gb SLC NAND flash, as read in iFixit's chip ID step (other teardowns read the memory differently)
Samsung K4B2G1646F-BYMA 2 Gb DDR3 memory, as read in iFixit's chip ID step (other teardowns read the memory differently)
MediaTek MT7658 Wi-Fi/Bluetooth combo chip, under a shield on the bottom board (iFixit)
Texas Instruments TAS2770 audio driver on the base board, amplifying the internal speaker (2019 teardown blog)
12 RGB LEDs around the outside edge of the top board (2019 teardown blog)
ISSI IS31FL3236 36-channel LED driver, controlled over I2C, driving the 12 RGB LEDs (2019 teardown blog)
Four microphones, part number given as UY19 2W07 (2019 teardown blog)
One 1.6-inch speaker (NaijaTechGuide spec page for the 3rd gen)
External plug-in power adapter supplied with the speaker, per a third-party repair blog: model GP92NB (LO P/N PA-1150-9ABN), input 110-240 V, 50-60 Hz, 0.5 A max; output 12 V, 1.25 A, 15 W
